If coverage changes: a unit test shows a successful sub-millisecond execution counts as covered, a genuinely missing execution still fails, and timing aggregation still excludes sub-millisecond values

context: Owner decision 2026-11-17: coverage counts every successful measurement execution regardless of duration; the 1 ms floor stays for timing aggregation only.
description:
## Problem
During PR #4260's CedarDB verification (mocker, TPC-H SF0.01, 3 streams, 132/132 queries passed), one sub-millisecond Q6 row tripped the stream-coverage check, so the result stayed unpublishable at that scale. A coverage check that treats a valid very fast query as missing would also misfire on fast engines at larger scales.

## Decision gate
Cause located: _throughput_measurement_queries (benchbox/validation/bundle.py ~2520, from #2921) drops successful rows with ms < 1.0, so a positive sub-millisecond timing is excluded from coverage on purpose. The same 1 ms usable-timing floor exists near bundle.py:1239 for timing aggregation. Decide whether coverage should count every successful measurement execution regardless of duration while keeping the 1 ms floor for aggregation, and confirm the published metrics stay consistent when a covered query has no usable timing. If the floor is the intended publication rule for coverage, the owner confirms it and the item closes with that reason.

## Guardrails
- A missing execution must still fail the coverage check; add a test for that case alongside the fast-query case.
- Do not lower timing resolution elsewhere.
